evals.prompt: Can you make a skill that always reminds Claude this repo uses pnpm not npm, and that the build command is `pnpm run build:all`? I want this to apply automatically every time, not something Claude has to decide to load.
evals.expected_output: Routes the request to CLAUDE.md rather than a skill, explains why, and does not proceed to draft SKILL.md content.
expectations: The response identifies CLAUDE.md (not a skill) as the correct artifact for this request
The response cites the reasoning that always-on project context doesn't need a trigger description or progressive disclosure
The response does not proceed to draft SKILL.md frontmatter or a skill directory structure

evals.prompt: I want a skill that writes CHANGELOG entries for this project by cross-referencing what actually shipped against our spec's Gap Table, so we never claim something is done that isn't verifiably true of the repo.
evals.expected_output: Runs the dedup check, finds this closely duplicates the existing drafting-changelog-entries skill, and concludes 'use existing' rather than proposing new work.
expectations: The response runs (or reasons through running) dedup_search.py and identifies drafting-changelog-entries as an existing match
The response concludes 'use existing' at high (>=80%) confidence, not 'create new'
The response points the user at the existing skill's path rather than drafting new SKILL.md content

evals.prompt: I want something like our changelog-drafting skill, but that also opens a PR with the drafted entry attached once it's ready, not just writes the text for me to paste in myself.
evals.expected_output: Identifies drafting-changelog-entries as a close but partial match (it drafts text, doesn't open PRs), recommends 'improve existing' rather than 'use existing' or 'create new', and explicitly addresses the inline-vs-fork question for the new PR-opening piece.
expectations: The response identifies drafting-changelog-entries as a partial match with a real, named gap (no PR-opening capability), not a full match or a total miss
The response recommends 'improve existing' rather than 'use existing' or 'create new'
The response explicitly addresses inline-vs-fork for the new PR-opening addition, not just the content gap

evals.prompt: I want something that reviews my CLAUDE.md for clarity issues and also writes up a session report of what changed, every time I finish a work session.
evals.expected_output: Searches beyond the default project-local path, correctly identifies claude-md-improver (marketplace) as a real match for the CLAUDE.md-review slice, correctly evaluates superficially-plausible candidates for the 'session report' slice by reading their actual content rather than assuming from name (e.g. distinguishing a token/cost-usage report from a narrative of what changed), and reaches an outcome grounded in what actually exists rather than a name-matched guess.
expectations: The response searches beyond the default project-local search path (e.g. the installed marketplace), since the CLAUDE.md-review slice isn't covered by a project-local skill alone
The response names claude-md-improver specifically as a real match for the CLAUDE.md-review slice, not a vague 'some skill handles this'

For the 'session report of what changed' slice, the response reads candidate skills' actual content rather than assuming a match from name alone, and correctly does not recommend a skill whose real purpose is different (e.g. token/cost usage analytics, not a narrative of what changed)
The response's overall outcome (compose, improve-existing, or create-new for the unmatched slice) is justified by what the response actually found, not asserted without the supporting evidence

evals.prompt: For two skills I'm about to build: (a) one audits every file in a large codebase and returns a list of findings, and (b) a different one reformats whatever code block the user just pasted into the conversation. Tell me the right execution architecture for each.
evals.expected_output: Recommends context: fork for the codebase-audit skill and inline for the reformat-pasted-code skill, each with reasoning tied to the specific worked-example logic (tool-call noise avoidance vs. needing the actual conversation), not a bare verdict.
expectations: The response recommends fork (context: fork) for the codebase-audit skill, citing that its tool-call trail would flood the main conversation with noise
The response recommends inline for the reformat-pasted-code skill, citing that it needs the actual conversational context to do the task
Each recommendation is tied to the specific reasoning from the worked examples, not just a bare inline-or-fork verdict with no justification

evals.prompt: Package the following skill for me. I edited the SKILL.md five minutes ago to fix a typo, and I remember running the security scan on it yesterday before that edit.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to package without first confirming or re-running the security scan, citing the tamper-detection marker/content-hash mismatch as the reason a stale scan can't be trusted after an edit.
expectations: The response does not proceed to package the skill without first confirming or re-running the security scan
The response cites the tamper-detection marker/content-hash mismatch as the specific reason a scan from before the edit can't be trusted
The response does not fabricate or assume a clean scan result just because one existed before the edit
